details: CONFIRMED by two scratch tests built on the change's own test base. The design (6.1) says the sha is "the newest commit of the landed
range that changes a non-inert file"; the code takes the newest commit reachable from the tip, and taking the default branch by a
merge commit (CLAUDE.md Git rule; live master history shows "Merge master into wt/core-leftover", "... wt/rename", "... wt/front-cmds")
puts other changes' commits there. The queue record then names the wrong change as the evidence a feature was done: corrupt data in
ordinary use. The landing pattern _branch_name matches wt/x anywhere in the subject, so "Merge master into wt/x" is taken as the
landing too.
Size: 30 agent minutes.
evidence: git log master --merges -n 8 --format=%s: "Merge master into wt/core-leftover", "Merge master into wt/rename", ...
failing_case: Feature feat taken by wt/feat; own commit A (lib/feat.py); master then gets commit Y (lib/other.py, another change); wt/feat takes
master by a merge commit "Merge master into wt/feat" (the rule before every landing); landing by fast-forward.
(a) ref kept: close_landed records evidence = Y (master's commit), not A: _newest_real_commit walks `git log --no-merges <tip>`,
which includes every commit master brought in.
(b) ref deleted after the landing (the merge hook's cleanup on the same command): landing() returns the newest merge commit whose
subject names wt/feat, which is "Merge master into wt/feat"; its diff against its first parent is master's changes, so
_commit_on_default accepts it and the evidence is that merge.
Should be: A (the newest non-inert commit of the branch's own line), or for a rider its "Merge wt/x into train-n" commit.
fix_hint: Walk the branch's own line: `git log --first-parent --no-merges <tip>` (stop at the commit where the branch left the default branch,
e.g. the merge-base before the landing or the take time), so merged-in master commits are skipped. In landing(), match only subjects
that merge wt/x INTO something ("Merge wt/x into", "Merge branch 'wt/x' into"), never "Merge ... into wt/x".
pass_cases: 1. Case (a) above: evidence == A.
2. Case (b) above: evidence == A, or the landing is reported without a sha and not closed with the master merge.
3. No master merge, tip an inert check commit, ref kept: evidence == the commit before the check (the change's existing test, keeps passing).
4. Train rider merged as "Merge wt/rider into train-1", ref deleted: evidence == that merge commit (existing test, keeps passing).
5. "Merge master into wt/x" and "Merge branch 'master' into wt/x" subjects never count as the landing of wt/x.
reason: tests/test_lanes_state.py:348, :354, :370 pass, fail without the fix.
findings.summary: a landed feature is closed with another change's commit as its evidence once the branch has taken the default branch

details: CONFIRMED that the ref-gone fast-forward path closes nothing (scratch J.test_ff_landing_then_branch_removed). PLAUSIBLE that the race
is lost in practice: both hooks fire on `git merge --ff-only wt/<x>`; merge.py's clean() is a few git calls, lanes.py runs a full
lanes_state (2.1 s measured live) before it looks. Every master landing in the newest 400 reflog entries is a fast-forward. The
"landed, still open" line is the backstop, so the front sees it; it is still a promise of 6.1 (features close at their landing)
that fails in the common landing form.
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: lines ['feat: landed, but git no longer shows its commit; close it by hand with `relay queue done feat --evidence <sha>`']
git reflog show master -n 400 | grep -ci fast-forward -> 400

failing_case: Feature feat taken by wt/feat, one own commit, no master merge; `git merge --ff-only wt/feat` on master; plugins/relay/hooks/merge.py
(PostToolUse on the same Bash command, run beside lanes.py) removes the worktree and `branch -d wt/feat`. If the removal finishes before
lanes.py reads the ref, landing() finds only the reflog line "merge wt/feat: Fast-forward" and returns sha None; close_landed prints
"landed, but git no longer shows its commit; close it by hand" and the feature stays taken.
Should be: closed with the commit the reflog entry moved master to (or the newest non-inert commit behind it).
fix_hint: Read the reflog with `--format=%H %gs` and, for the matching "merge wt/x: Fast-forward" entry, use %H (the tip master moved to) with
the same first-parent walk as F2's fix to find the newest non-inert commit.

2. FF landing, branch kept: closed as today.
3. A branch dropped without landing (ref gone, no reflog line): stays taken, listed "(gone, item still taken)" (existing test).

details: CONFIRMED with a scratch repository: a commit dated 2026-10-01, a branch made from it now: `git reflog show --format='%ct %gs' -n 1`
prints 1790812800 (1 Oct) beside "branch: Created from master" while now is 1793160712. The entry's own time needs the reflog
selector date (`--date=unix --format=%gd` gives wt/y@{<epoch>}). The change's test passes only because its seed commit is made seconds
before the worktree.
Size: 10 agent minutes.

committer date of the commit the entry points to (4 h ago), so wt/y is "quiet", not running, and the line and the Stop hook offer its
lane as free.
Should be: running for lane_quiet_hours from its creation (the design: "newest branch reflog entry").
fix_hint: `git reflog show --date=unix --format=%gd -n 1 refs/heads/<branch>` and parse the number between "@{" and "}".
pass_cases: 1. Commit dated 27 days ago, `git worktree add -b wt/y` now, no file changed: wt/y running at now, quiet at now + 4 h (setting 3).
2. A worktree with a file changed now: running (existing test).
3. A worktree whose newest reflog entry and files are 4 h old: listed "(quiet)" (existing test).
